The 2016 PDFs print CT, ET and UTC themselves and are quoted as printed, including CME's own defects (the MLK PDF's '17100 ET' typo is on a line the task does not quote, so nothing was silently corrected).

summary: matches=false. Retrieval integrity is excellent: 106/106 stored hashes reproduce, eight re-fetched documents are byte-identical, every verbatim the task quotes is faithful to the bytes it cites (two trivial transcription slips aside), no instant is inferred from another year, ET=CT+1 holds on all 363 rows, and a fresh CDX enumeration of 2018 reproduces the saved one capture-for-capture. The dataset fails on SOURCE SELECTION, not transcription: the task used CME's own annual holiday-calendar bundle to obtain the final 2016 revisions, then never tried the 2017 or 2018 bundles, both of which are archived and both of which carry later CME revisions than the per-file captures it served. That single omission (a) invents a gap that does not exist -- the 2017 Christmas sheet's final revision prints the Bitcoin row the task recorded as 'unknown'; (b) leaves a wrong Cryptocurrency status on 2018-07-03; (c) serves a withdrawn Monday-evening grain leg on 2017-12-25 while correctly withholding the identical leg on 2018-01-01; and (d) makes the 'channels tried' claims in missing[0] and missing[6] false. Items 1-5 are load-bearing and must be fixed; 6-8 are moderate; 9-11 are minor.
